trigger_condition: `set --path workstreams --replace` is accepted because the rejection covers only paths longer than one segment; the parent map is not a documented replaceable node and skips every workstream guard.

potential_consequence: A workstream can be written as `done` without `done`'s evidence and overlay checks; reproduced with a full node: the write returns ok and `validate` stays clean.

trigger_condition: `set --path bmad --value '{"model":"current"}'` replaces the whole `bmad` block with no `--replace` and no `--reason`, and accepts a model the scalar `bmad.model` path rejects.
guard_snippet: Add `bmad` to `replace_required` and a `bmad` branch to `_validate_value` that validates the model and keeps `memlog` and the three output paths as strings.
potential_consequence: The audit trail silently moves to the default path once the recorded `memlog` is dropped: reproduced with `init --memlog audit.md`; later writes land in `.memlog.md` while `validate` stays clean.

trigger_condition: The documented switch `set --path active_workstream --value <id>` sets the target status to `active` unconditionally, so a `done` workstream reopens with no reason.
guard_snippet: Refuse activating a done workstream, or route the transition through the same guarded status write at 2835-2842.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: a closed workstream becomes active with `validate` clean and only `root active_workstream updated` in the audit trail; the close reason is never revisited.

trigger_condition: The done-workstream reopen guard fires only when the target is `active`; `status paused` downgrades a done workstream with no reason, after which `active` also needs none.
guard_snippet: Require `--reason` for any transition whose current workstream status is `done`, whatever the target status.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: `done` -> `paused` -> `active` returns ok twice, `validate` is clean, and no reason is recorded anywhere.

trigger_condition: There is no workstream analogue of `_guard_active_phase`: `set --workstream ws-001 --path status --value active` leaves an already-active ws-002 active.
guard_snippet: Add `_guard_active_workstream` that refuses a second active workstream or pauses the previous one, as the `active_workstream` branch already does.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: the command returns `ok: true`, then `validate` errors `only one workstream may be active at a time`; the tool reports success for a ledger it rejects.

trigger_condition: `_guard_phase_status` never checks the workstream status, so a phase can be reopened on a `done` workstream without reopening the workstream first.
guard_snippet: At the top of `_guard_phase_status`, fail any phase reopen when `workstream.status == "done"`, as `gate-matrix.md` §Reopening requires.
potential_consequence: Reproduced on a genuinely closed ledger: `phases.build` becomes `active` while the workstream stays `done`; `validate` reports no error and the dashboard shows a closed workstream with an open phase.

trigger_condition: `cmd_ticket` refuses every write on a done workstream, while `cmd_set` guards only a reopen; passing a still-open optional gate after close is accepted.
guard_snippet: Apply the same done-workstream refusal in `cmd_set`, or state which writes are allowed after close and record them as a post-close event.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: `set ... gates.close.retro.status passed` on a closed workstream returns ok and `validate` is clean; the close summary and the gate record now disagree, and the two commands enforce opposite policies.

trigger_condition: A decided gate cannot move to `passed` with `--reason` (the flag is rejected for a passed gate), and the same write without a reason is rejected as a reopen, so the documented transition is unreachable.
guard_snippet: Allow `--reason` when the current status is decided and the target is `passed`; otherwise name the two-step workaround in the error and the docs.
potential_consequence: Reproduced for `set` and `ticket`: skipped/overridden -> passed always fails, contradicting `gate-matrix.md` §Reopening ("moves again only with `--reason`, whichever status it moves to").

trigger_condition: The phase `done`/`skipped` check exists only in the `kind == "phase"` branch, so a ticket gate can reopen to `open` while `phases.build` is already done.
guard_snippet: Before the ticket-ordering block, fail a ticket-gate reopen to `open` when the build phase is `done`/`skipped`, with the same "reopen the phase first" message.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: the write returns ok, then `summary` reports `complete: false` for a phase still marked done and `validate` errors `phases.build is done with undecided gates`.

trigger_condition: `_guard_decided_metadata` finds the gate with `_node_at`, which splits the path on every dot, so a dotted ticket id resolves to the wrong node and the guard no-ops.
guard_snippet: Resolve the node with the ticket-aware logic used by `get_parent`/`_ticket_gate_index`, for example through `_gate_status_target(path)` and an explicit ticket-map lookup.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: `set --path tickets.1.3.gates.review.override_reason --null` and the `decided_at` twin both return ok on an overridden gate; `validate` then errors that the override has no reason.

trigger_condition: The phase-done guard checks gates but not `cmd_done`'s rule that a non-audit build phase needs a ticket, so `set phases.build.status done` succeeds on an empty build.
guard_snippet: Mirror `cmd_done`'s `phase == "build" and not tickets and track != "audit"` check in `_guard_phase_status`.
potential_consequence: Reproduced on a fresh fix/one-session ledger: the write returns ok, then `validate` errors `phases.build is done with no ticket built`; the phase cache claims a build that never happened.

trigger_condition: `_written_gate` returns None for a whole `tickets.<id>` node, so the documented node-replacement form skips `_guard_reopen`, `_guard_ticket_order`, and `_guard_blocked_gate` for every gate inside the node.
guard_snippet: Expand a whole-ticket node write into the same per-gate checks before writing, or reject gate-bearing ticket-node replacements in favour of `ticket`.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: replacing T1 with `review: open` and `done: passed` returns ok while the identical change through `ticket` is refused; a blocked review can also be recorded passed, and `validate` then errors.

trigger_condition: `cmd_done` builds its blocking list from `phase_blocking`, which accepts any decided status, and never re-checks gate order before writing `status: done`.
guard_snippet: Before closing, re-run the per-ticket invariants `validate` enforces (done passed requires review passed, review decided requires ticket decided).
potential_consequence: Reproduced end to end: `done --accept-missing-evidence --accept-missing-tickets --reason ...` closes a ledger whose `done` is passed while `review` is skipped, and `validate` still errors afterwards.

trigger_condition: The unknown-ticket check accepts any prefix match, and `get_parent` falls back to the longest existing id, so with ticket `1` present, `tickets.1.3` writes a nested `"3"` under ticket `1`.
guard_snippet: Resolve an exact ticket id against the map and fail when no key matches the remaining segments; `get_parent` should only accept ids `_validate_path` validated.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: `set --path tickets.1.3 --replace --reason probe --value '{"title":"phantom"}'` returns ok and writes `tickets['1']['3']`; `validate` stays clean and a real `1.3` can later coexist.

trigger_condition: The scalar path rejects `phases.<phase>.gate` as derived, but a whole-phase node write accepts `gate` and the phase field list also admits undefined `decided_at`/`override_reason` fields.
guard_snippet: Reject `gate` in the `phases` len==2 branch of `_validate_value`, and narrow the phase allowlist to `status`, `evidence`, and `note`.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: a node write stores `gate: optional` where the resolver says `required`, and `validate` reports drift; the scalar form returns `phases.<phase>.gate is derived`.

trigger_condition: `_guard_phase_status` enforces the gate bullets of `gate-matrix.md` §Phase completion but not bullet 4, that the phase's evidence pointers are set.
guard_snippet: Before accepting `done`, require phase evidence or a decided gate's artifact pointer, reusing the `ARTIFACT_GATES` check `cmd_done` performs at 3216-3248.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: every plan gate is passed with no artifact or evidence anywhere, `set phases.plan.status done` returns ok, and `validate` is clean; the missing evidence is only discovered later at `done`.

trigger_condition: `resize` calls `apply_levels`, which flips a `done`/`skipped` phase to `pending` when the new size demands open gates; `resize` takes no `--reason` and its audit line omits the reopened phases.
guard_snippet: Require `--reason` when `apply_levels` reopens a phase, and name the reopened phases in the resize event.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: resizing a fix/one-session ledger to epic changes `phases.plan` from `skipped` to `pending`; the persisted trail only says `resized to track=fix size=epic`, so the reopen has no reason and no explanation.

trigger_condition: `--delete` has no workstream-status check, so a ticket can be removed from a closed workstream (or the synthetic `audit` ticket can be removed).
guard_snippet: Refuse `--delete` when the workstream is done, and refuse deleting the `audit` ticket on an audit workstream.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: deleting T1 from a closed workstream returns ok and `validate` stays clean; deleting the audit ticket leaves a ledger `validate` rejects with `tickets.audit is required for an audit`.

trigger_condition: Whole-ticket node validation requires `len(parts) == 2`, so a dotted id (`tickets.1.3`) skips the gate-name and status checks.
guard_snippet: Resolve the ticket id from the map, then apply the ticket-node checks whenever the path names one existing ticket.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: a `tickets.1.3` replacement with an unknown gate name and status `whatever` returns ok; `validate` then rejects the ledger.

trigger_condition: `--delete` compares a string id against the raw map keys, so a hand-edited integer-keyed ticket is never found.
guard_snippet: Compare `str(ticket_id)` against `{str(key) for key in ticket_map}`, as `done` already normalizes ids.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: a ticket keyed `7` is refused with `--delete is only for an existing whole ticket node`; `ticket` then creates a second string-keyed entry.

trigger_condition: `resolve_memlog` returns `Path(args.memlog).resolve()` without `expand_project_root`, although `SKILL.md:17` and `ledger-schema.md:290` say every command expands `--memlog`.
guard_snippet: Pass `args.memlog` through `expand_project_root` in `resolve_memlog`, matching `cmd_init`.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: `--memlog '{project-root}/audit2.md'` creates a literal `{project-root}/` directory under the cwd and writes there instead of the project root.

trigger_condition: `--delete` allows removing the synthetic `audit` ticket, which the ledger requires for an audit's review gate.
guard_snippet: Refuse `--delete` for `tickets.audit` on an audit workstream (or reject the delete when the ticket is synthetic).
potential_consequence: Reproduced: the delete returns ok; `validate` then errors `workstreams.ws-001.tickets.audit is required for an audit`.

trigger_condition: A path with an unknown dotted id whose prefix is an existing ticket is accepted, and the write lands as a nested node under the prefix.
guard_snippet: Require the resolved ticket id to match a key exactly; otherwise fail and point at `ticket`.
potential_consequence: Reproduced: `tickets.1.3` writes `tickets['1']['3']`; `validate` stays clean, so the phantom survives. (Same root cause as the adversarial finding.)

trigger_condition: `_guard_decided_metadata` is exercised only through a dotless phase gate, so the dotted-id no-op introduced by making dotted ids writable is untested.
guard_snippet: Add `test_set_refuses_to_clear_a_decided_override_reason_on_a_dotted_ticket`: create `1.3`, override `review`, then `set --path tickets.1.3.gates.review.override_reason --null` must fail; add the `decided_at` twin.
potential_consequence: The documented dotted-id `set` form can erase an audited reason and the suite stays green; only a later `validate` notices.
consumer: `set --path tickets.<dotted-id>.gates.<gate>.override_reason|decided_at --null`, the write form unlocked in round 3.
evidence: `test_set_refuses_to_clear_a_decided_override_reason` (test_sdlc_plan.py:2815-2838) uses `gates.plan.ux`; grep for `_node_at` finds one call site and no ticket path. Reproduced the failure against a throwaway ledger.

trigger_condition: The done-workstream branch of `_guard_reopen` is never executed: its only test drives `ticket`, which the new `cmd_ticket` refusal shadows.
guard_snippet: Add a `set` case after `done`: `set --path tickets.T1.gates.done.status --value open --reason rework` and a phase-gate twin must both fail with `cannot reopen a gate on a done workstream`.
potential_consequence: Removing lines 2591-2595 leaves the suite green while `set` reopens a gate on a closed workstream, and `validate` then rejects the ledger.
consumer: `set --path <phase-or-ticket-gate>.status`, the write form loop step 5 uses for phase gates.
evidence: `test_reopening_a_gate_on_a_done_workstream_is_refused` (test_sdlc_plan.py:2081-2123) asserts `workstream is done`, which is `cmd_ticket` at 3016; grep for `cannot reopen a gate on a done workstream` in the suite returns nothing.

trigger_condition: The `active_workstream` switch reopens a done workstream with no reason; no test covers that path after a close.
guard_snippet: Add: after `done`, `set --path active_workstream --value ws-001` must fail, and the guarded `set --path status --value active --reason ...` must succeed.
potential_consequence: The `resume <workstream>` path silently reopens closed history; `validate` stays clean and the audit records only a generic update.
evidence: The two tests that exercise the path (test_sdlc_plan.py:1463-1479, 2542-2569) use non-done workstreams; reproduced the silent reopen after `done`.

trigger_condition: The reason required to reopen a done workstream is validated and then discarded: the status path falls into the generic `status updated` branch, while the phase twin writes `(reason: ...)`.
guard_snippet: Emit the reason on the workstream-status event and assert it, e.g. `assertIn("ws-001 status=active (reason: reopen for rework)", trail.read_text())`.
potential_consequence: The justification for reopening a closed workstream never reaches the audit trail, and deleting the whole reason plumbing keeps the suite green.
consumer: The audit trail read by a post-hoc reviewer of a reopened workstream (`gate-matrix.md` §Reopening names this command).
evidence: Reproduced: `set --workstream ws-001 --path status --value active --reason "reopen for rework"` logs `ws-001 status updated`; `test_reopening_a_done_workstream_needs_a_reason` (test_sdlc_plan.py:2125-2175) ends at `assertTrue(accepted["ok"])` and never reads the memlog.

trigger_condition: Whole-ticket node replacement is validated for gate names only; the guards keyed on `_written_gate` return None for a ticket node, and no test writes one.

potential_consequence: Round 3's blocked-gate bypass survives one node up; the node form can record a blocked review as passed and `validate` then errors.
consumer: `set --path tickets.<id>` whole-node replacement, a documented `set` form in `references/ledger-schema.md` §set rules.
evidence: The only `tickets.T1` write in the suite is the delete test (test_sdlc_plan.py:2348); `test_set_node_write_requires_replace_and_respects_phase_guard` (1638-1662) writes only `phases.close`. Reproduced both failures.

trigger_condition: Only `init` and `done` are tested for `{project-root}` expansion and for a bad root; the new expansion and `is_dir` refusal in `detect`, `reconcile`, and `verify-return` are unexecuted.

potential_consequence: A regression in any of those expansions ships green while the activation and loop commands that pass the literal token fail hard.
consumer: activation step 6 and loop step 4, which pass `--project-root {project-root}` (`SKILL.md:63-68`, 91-93) relying on the expansion promise.
evidence: grep for `{project-root}` in the suite finds only `test_init_expands_the_project_root_token` and `test_done_expands_the_project_root_token`; grep for `project root not found` finds no test although the script fails with it in five commands.

trigger_condition: Only the `accepted missing ticket artifact for:` close-note branch is asserted; the `accepted missing evidence:` and `accepted tickets absent from BMAD artifacts:` branches are unpinned.
guard_snippet: Assert the evidence branch in `test_done_requires_evidence_and_its_accept_flag_needs_a_reason`, and the stale-ticket branch in `test_reconcile_and_done_report_ticket_overlay_drift`.
potential_consequence: Two of the three lines answering "what was waived at close" can be deleted with the suite green, restoring the round-3 audit gap for those cases.
consumer: the close audit line for `done --accept-missing-evidence` and for stale ledger tickets.
evidence: `test_done_names_the_accepted_gap` (test_sdlc_plan.py:2396-2423) asserts only the ticket-artifact line; grep for `accepted missing evidence` and `accepted tickets absent` in the suite returns no hits.

trigger_condition: No rubric inspects the durable ledger or audit trail, so every case passes even if the skill writes nothing: the "no new workstream", "no ledger created" and "no code produced" rows are satisfied by silence in the final message.
guard_snippet: Add one artifact assertion per case (for example `plan.yaml` exists with the reported track/size, or does not exist for status-only requests) and assert the phase note for a blocked action.
potential_consequence: The eval suite cannot distinguish a correct plan write from a correct-sounding message; the write loop is only covered by the unit suite, and the README does not say the rubrics are text-only.
consumer: the 10 quality cases in `evals/cases.json`, all graded 62/62 in this review.
evidence: All ten `grading.json` files from the fresh run flag this; for example `start-greenfield` passed while every gate stayed open in `cwd/_bmad-output/sdlc/plan.yaml`, and `status-empty` passes with no ledger at all. The run wrote correct state, but no expectation reads it.

trigger_condition: The `continue-with-ledger` rubric never asserts the "work only in the project root" scope sentence, and the fresh run violated it by copying the ledger to `/private/tmp/sdlc-probe` and probing there.
guard_snippet: Add a scope expectation (no write outside `cwd`) or stage a read-only marker; keep the sentence in `prompt.txt` as well as `case.json`.
potential_consequence: A scope violation passes the case; the same rubric gives no signal that the conductor left the project root while handling a ledger.
evidence: The transcript contains `sdlc-probe` three times and the grader noted the copy; the rubric has no path assertion, and the case input sentence is present in `case.json` but not in the generated `prompt.txt`.

trigger_condition: No test covers `--delete` on a done workstream, deletion of the synthetic audit ticket, or the phase reopen performed by `resize`.
guard_snippet: Add delete-after-close, delete-audit, and resize-reopens-a-skipped-phase cases, asserting both the refusal and the audit line.

evidence: grep for `--delete` in the suite finds only `test_set_delete_removes_a_ticket` (test_sdlc_plan.py:2348); no test resizes a workstream with a skipped/done phase or deletes `tickets.audit`.
